answer: A zephyr guards an agent economy with a terrace staircase of falling plumes: every new identity must catch one plume on each terrace it climbs, and the terraces double each time, so the first fake climbs 3 terraces, the second 6, the third 12, the tenth 1,536 and the twentieth 1,572,864, and twenty fakes together climb 3,145,725. Bulk farming fails because one zephyr blows one plume at a time and each terrace's plume can only be caught after the last one lands, so no plume can be caught early, in parallel, or bought; like a juggler catching feathers in a breeze, one at a time.
